messages:
incident-bot: :rotating_light: ALERT: Service "inference-prod" in az1a reporting 5xx spike and TCP RSTs to GPU nodes. Src: controlplane health-checks fail. Root TS: 3755012345
Carla: I'm oncall. seeing ~12% 5xx for inference-prod, p95 latency up from 120ms -> 1.3s. Customers A/B are affected. Kicking off investigation.
Alice: I'm pulling health checks and node metrics. netstat on gpu-pool shows bursts of RSTs, tx-queue growth on eni-0. Packet drops correlate with host transmit queue length.
Ben: Runtime reports KV cache misses rising and model shards timing out at RPC layer. Retries causing fanout amplification.
Dan: AWS side: ENI tx_skb backlog seen in kernel logs on hosts in az1a. Could be host NIC scheduler issue or driver. Checking host-level kmsg and dmesg.
Carla: For immediate mitigation, let's shift traffic away from az1a for inference-prod. Run steering now? :arrow_right:
Alice: Agreed. Suggest traffic-split to eu-west-2 and us-west-2 variants at 60/40 to absorb load. Update route policy with lower weight for az1a.
Ben: Can we apply model variant fallback to smaller shard size to reduce RPC contention? I can push a canary config to 10% before broader switch.
Carla: Do the smaller shard fallback first; then start traffic steer. Need smoke verification after each step.
Ben: Pushing config now:
```
# rollout
redwood route update inference-prod --weight az1a=10,eu-west-2=45,us-west-2=45 --force
redwood model set inference-model-prod --fallback small-shard --canary 10
```
Alice: Verified runtime logs show reduced timeouts on the canary nodes, p50 back to ~150ms for canary traffic.
Dan: On hosts: kernel shows repeated "tx queue full" and "NETDEV WATCHDOG" for eni-0. I'm opening a ticket with AWS networking team for host NIC driver investigation. In-flight hosts are being cordoned.
Carla: Cordoning/evicting affected nodes. Command:
```
kubectl cordon node/gpu-az1a-07
kubectl drain node/gpu-az1a-07 --ignore-daemonsets --delete-local-data
```
Alice: Drained two nodes so far, controller rescheduled pods to other AZs. Observed a small ramp in latency for those reschedules but steady overall.
Eva: Customer Success: Notifying top impacted customers (Customer A, Customer B). ETA for mitigation is immediate traffic shift + node drains. Drafting message for CS - will push in 10m.
Frank: Product: Which SLAs triggered? Need to capture affected volume and map to committed latency SLOs for postmortem.
Carla: Current impact estimate: 11-14% requests failing for az1a traffic window, overall product-level error rate peaked at 8%. We'll capture request ids and correlate.
Alice: Logs: sample error IDs -> 7fa3b2c9, 7fa3b2d0, 7fa3b2e1 (stack includes rpc timeout and econnreset). Saving to /var/log/incidents/3755012345/errors.log
Dan: AWS ticket opened: 1234567890. AWS confirmed seeing host-level NIC interrupts; they suggested switching instance placement to different hypervisor or moving to different AZ while they investigate.
Carla: Short-term plan: keep reduced weight on az1a (10%) and continue draining unstable hosts. Long-term: repro/firm root cause with AWS and schedule replacement of affected capacity pool.
Alice: Post-mitigation numbers: overall 5xx down to 1.2%, p95 latency back to 210ms. Will monitor for 30m to confirm stability.
Eva: Notified customers: initial message sent. Will update with resolution note once stable.
Ben: Runtime will keep the small-shard fallback enabled until AWS confirms hosts are healthy. Rolling back to normal shards only after full stability.
Frank: Capturing actions for postmortem: timeline, traffic steer commands, node drains, AWS ticket id, CS comms. I'll own coordinating the postmortem doc.
Carla: Thanks everyone. If error spikes again, we'll re-open page. For now monitoring only. :white_check_mark:
incident-bot: Incident updated: status=mitigated, severity=high -> monitoring. Links: runbook/incidents/az-network-queue
